evidence.excerpt:
Artificial intelligence (AI) scientists pursue discovery through a chain of hypotheses, fitting candidate
models to existing observations and often choosing experiments where those models disagree most. Yet when
early data miss a narrow feature, model selection favors simple curves that agree across the unmeasured gap,
so disagreement-guided search has no reason to look where the new phenomenon lies. When we tested two
frontier AI scientists, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol, across 32 closed-loop trials with a narrow peak
omittedfromthestartingdata,bothsampledinsidethepeakregionlessoftenthanrandomsearch. Surprisingly,
the agent that followed model disagreement more closely missed the peak in all 32 trials, whereas discovery
succeeded when experiments probed the unmeasured gap early and followed up across the anomaly. Asking
the right question, rather than testing only where current

evidence.excerpt:
and standard
model selection penalizes extra parameters until the data show a clear departure24. Simple models fitted to
the observed background then agree across the unmeasured gap and differ only over minor details elsewhere.
Following their disagreement steers experiments away from that gap rather than into it, much as confirmation
bias keeps human researchers testing what their working theories already anticipate25–27.
To test how experimental choices shape autonomous discovery, we evaluated two frontier AI scientists,
Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol, in closed-loop equation-discovery trials where a narrow peak lay inside
an initially unmeasured region. Both agents probed that region less often than random search, and the
agent that followed equation disagreement more closely missed the peak in every trial as it spent its budget
separating nearly identical background curves. By

In our closed-loop task, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol sought to discover an unknown equation
𝑦=𝑓(𝑥 1,𝑥 2,𝑥 3)+𝜀 over 12 rounds of experiments (Fig. 1a and Methods). In this system,𝑦 rises and levels
off with𝑥1, decays smoothly with𝑥2, and does not depend on𝑥3. Hidden inside that smooth decay is a narrow
Gaussian peak region𝑊 covering 7%of the𝑥2 range. At𝑥1 =40 ,𝑦 rises up to31𝜎 above the smooth curve
inside𝑊 (in units of measurement noise𝜎) while adding less than2𝜎 anywhere outside𝑊. Across 32 paired
trials with different peak locations along𝑥2, both agents received the same four random starting conditions
outside𝑊, so the initial data showed only the smooth background.
In each round, the agent saw all measurements collected so far alongside its best-fitting equations
from earlier rounds, ranked by the Bayesian information

First, the measurement inside𝑊 had to stand out clearly from the smooth background before BIC would
favor adding extra parameters (Fig. 3a). Because the peak tapers toward the edges of𝑊 and scales with𝑥1,
experiments near the boundary of𝑊 or at low𝑥1 produced only modest departures. When a measurement hit
the peak strongly (≥10𝜎 , 19of the32entered trials), the large error overturned the smooth fit and launched a

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final recovery was scored against held-out ground-truth test points, and search behavior was additionally compared with equation-free baselines (random sampling and interval bisection).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcome is the final RMSE/sigma score computed on 4,096 fixed uniform random held-out test points from the ground-truth function, with success defined as E <= 1.05.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Candidate equations were fitted and ranked by BIC from bounded nonlinear least squares on observed measurements, and the agents' experimental choices were guided by disagreement among these BIC-ranked equations.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The experimental evidence directly supports the headline claims: agents relying strongly on model disagreement underfit and under-sample unobserved regions, whereas broader initial exploratory sampling is required to seed the multi-step chain of hypotheses needed for recovery.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation thoroughly compares agent search trajectories against explicit baselines (random search and interval bisection), quantifying sampling frequencies inside the hidden feature region and measuring equation disagreement dynamics with appropriate statistical tests (McNemar, Fisher exact, Wilcoxon signed-rank).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final model recovery was verified against 4,096 held-out ground-truth test points as well as comparison against independent exploration baselines (random sampling and interval bisection).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The final success metric is root-mean-square prediction error normalized by noise standard deviation (RMSE/sigma <= 1.05) evaluated across 4,096 held-out uniform random test points generated from the ground-truth function.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: During the closed-loop trials, candidate equations were ranked by the Bayesian information criterion (BIC) based on bounded nonlinear least squares fits to observed experimental measurements.

primary.limitations: The study clearly articulates its focus on a controlled synthetic three-variable regression system without code execution or external tool use, appropriately bounding the generalization of its findings to higher-dimensional or physical lab settings.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is rigorous and well-controlled, using a 12-round closed-loop experimental design across 32 paired synthetic discovery trials with identical starting observations, fixed noise levels, and objective nonlinear fitting pipelines for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a clear, scoped, and well-executed empirical contribution to understanding the active-learning and hypothesis-generation behavior of modern LLM agents, supported by rigorous experimental controls, sound statistical reporting, and transparent discussion of limitations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript demonstrates and analyzes a blind-spot failure mode in closed-loop AI scientific discovery where model-disagreement-guided exploration combined with complexity penalization (BIC) prevents LLM agents from detecting localized unmeasured features.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a clear, scoped, and well-executed empirical contribution to understanding the active-learning and hypothesis-generation behavior of modern LLM agents, supported by rigorous experimental controls, sound statistical reporting, and transparent discussion of limitations.
